text:
maria: Quick sketch + question — proposing we collapse the left index into three primary headings (Project, Models, Observability) and turn other items into contextual flyouts. Idea is to reduce visual noise and make deep links more predictable for product pages. Thoughts?

sam: fewer top-level items sounds good to me. main concern: breadcrumb stability when things are collapsed. Users expect a stable path copy/paste.

lina: agree on stability. If we collapse, breadcrumbs should still reflect the full logical path, not the collapsed label. e.g. show: `Org > Project X > Model > Versions` even if sidebar shows just “Models”.

alex: +1. We also need to be explicit about permalink format. Current routes are messy: `#/m/abc` vs `/orgs/:org/projects/:p/models/:id`. Can we standardize on full-path URLs (no hashes) and use URL query for ephemeral states?

maria: that's the ask — canonical full-paths w/ hash only for small UI state. Example proposals I mocked: `https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/redwood/projects/rosetta/models/rosetta-7b?panel=metrics` and `https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/redwood/projects/rosetta#breadcrumbs=compact`

ethan: accessibility nits: when we collapse, keyboard focus order must follow the breadcrumb and not the visual collapsed group. Also ensure the live region announces when focus lands in a flyout.

sam: behavior question — when user clicks a subitem in a collapsed group, do we expand the group and navigate, or navigate directly while keeping groups collapsed? which preserves context?

lina: navigate directly (keep collapsed) is better for vertical space, but the animation should briefly show which group contains the target so context isn’t lost. Maybe small toast: `Found under Models` with `aria-live=polite`.

alex: Regarding deep links from external sources (docs, emails) — we must guarantee route backwards compatibility for at least 6 months. Suggest middleware that translates legacy hash routes to new canonical paths.

maria: good call. We can add routing shim: legacy -> canonical mapping table. Dev question: how expensive is maintaining that?

ethan: shim is straightforward if we log unmatched legacy routes for one month and then prune. Also add telemetry flag `legacy_route_handled=true` so we can alert if some routes are failing.

prod-bot: deploy-preview created: `preview/compact-sidebar-v2` at https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/compact-sidebar-v2 — includes routing shim + breadcrumb tests.

sam: I'll run an accessibility pass on the preview tomorrow. Quick checklist: 1) focus order 2) screenreader announcements for flyouts 3) link text specificity (avoid "click here") 4) keyboard expand/collapse.

lina: copy tweak: instead of “Models” label maybe “Model hub” — clearer when collapsed. open to alternate words. also ensure breadcrumbs use the full resource names, not UI labels (so breadcrumbs remain stable for automation).

maria: love “Model hub” suggestion. We'll try it in the preview. One more UX question: when user bookmarks a sub-section (e.g., specific eval results), should the bookmark include the UI panel state? pros: reproducible view. cons: brittle across UI changes.

alex: prefer minimal bookmarks: canonical path + stable query keys (e.g., `?eval=123`). Avoid serializing ephemeral panel states. Document the supported query params so external tools can link reliably.

sam: last accessibility nit — ensure that when we change route programmatically (e.g., canonicalization redirect), we call `focus()` on the main heading and set `document.title` appropriately so screen reader users aren't lost.

maria: great feedback. Next steps: 1) ship preview to design + a11y 2) sam to run quick a11y sweep 3) dev to add legacy route telemetry 4) product to lock query param contract. I'll update the mock and post an updated screenshot. :sparkles:

ethan: thanks — will add aria-live prototypes to the preview.

alex: i'll draft the route migration doc (mapping table + deprecation timeline).

prod-bot: preview build passed e2e checks (2/2).
